Data source overview:  
The LessWrong post introduces “activation engineering”, a technique that steers GPT-2-XL at inference time by adding an activation vector to the residual stream.  A contrastively-derived steering vector doubled TruthfulQA accuracy, and several open problems are proposed (PCA-based directions, circuit-targeted additions, and understanding failure when the coefficient is too large).

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]  
Inference strategy justification:  The post explicitly links model mis-truthfulness to runtime steering via activation addition and reports quantitative TruthfulQA gains; risks and failure modes were lifted verbatim, while interventions for open problems were moderately inferred and therefore marked with low maturity and low edge confidence.  
Extraction completeness explanation:  All causal chains from the two explicit risks (untruthful answers and degradation from large coefficients) to every actionable intervention discussed or implied in the source are included, with intermediate concept nodes capturing methods, findings and hypotheses.  All nodes are interconnected through shared concepts (activation vector addition), satisfying mandatory success criteria.  
Key limitations:  Source is informal; quantitative evidence depth is limited, so some confidences are medium.  Open-problem interventions are speculative; future work could supply stronger empirical backing.
